localBiteReport: The most current available report for Choctawhatchee Bay is from the week of September 4–10, 2026 (about one week old as of today). According to Capt. Blake Nelson of Last Cast Charters, the bay is showing clear early signs of the fall transition, with large concentrations of baitfish pushing from open water into bayous, flats, and bridge areas. Redfish are the headline inshore story: sight-fishing opportunities on the flats are improving, and local guides expect the slot-red bite to pick up meaningfully from mid-to-late September onward as the fall mullet run gets underway — cut or butterfly-rigged finger mullet on a single-drop rig with an orange or pink bead is the anticipated setup. Water temperature is 86°F. Speckled trout are also reported active in the bay's grass flat areas, and captainexperiences.com trip reports from Santa Rosa Beach anglers (dated approximately 6 days before the report pull) note good numbers of speckled trout alongside bull redfish in the 26-lb class being landed.
